rationale: Ground truth has no substantive reviewer concerns (just an LGTM approval), so both trivially achieve full recall. X is tightly scoped and safely grounded, verifying diff claims against source with specific line refs and one appropriately hedged, low-risk comment, but offers little actionable follow-up. Y is more ambitious, surfacing a genuinely relevant sibling-doc inconsistency (README.md:59), a missing regression test, and an index-collision nit, each with concrete file/line targets and suggested fixes — more actionable, though its broader net of claims (extending into files/tests outside the diff) carries more unverified risk, pulling precision down slightly relative to X's narrower, safer approach.
